request: Show Users / Voices recordings in descending creation-date order, newest first.
behavior: The capture API orders by created_at DESC and id DESC, preserving a deterministic tie-breaker.
A bounded versioned cursor carries the exact float timestamp and fingerprint suffix. Later pages continue without duplicates if newer captures arrive or the boundary capture expires.
Legacy ID cursor syntax remains accepted when its boundary record still exists. New cursors do not require that record to remain stored.
REST capture limits and source/dependency budgets continue to use the last included chronological position when a page is cut short.
The view sorts recording rows globally by the same key. Voice groups no longer pull older member rows above newer recordings in another group.
Each visible group keeps its existing selection/correction controls, and each capture row identifies its group. Profiles and listening samples keep their existing retention flow.

cursor.format: vc1_<16 lowercase hexadecimal IEEE754 float64 timestamp characters>_<64 lowercase fingerprint hex characters>

source_validation.includes: New chronological API pagination, tied dates, a new arrival between pages, expired boundary records, invalid cursor payloads and existing voice grouping, review, registry, receipts and diagnostic-client regression cases.

frontend_validation.includes: Interleaved groups stay in chronological row order, tied dates match the server order, group selection still selects nonadjacent members, and existing voice privacy/retirement/controller tests pass.

first_current_attempt.failure: Timeout at the existing three-second independent idle-expiry ACK wait while source integration tests were also running.

chromium_validation.interpretation: The committed baseline and changed checkout both passed the complete existing Chromium test when run in isolation. The initial timeout was not reproduced; its precise cause has not been established.

release_status: Prepared in the development checkout; publication requires the agreed compiled-release flow.
